summary: How radios spread and share signals, turn voice into data and guard their bits: spread spectrum, TDMA, CODECs, layers, SDR, DSC and SITOR.

blocks.title: SSB and emission codes
items: Modulation puts a voice on a carrier, making 2 sidebands: copies of the voice.
SSB (single sideband) sends 1 sideband and suppresses the carrier, saving power and needing half the bandwidth.

blocks.title: Spread spectrum
items: Spread spectrum: a wide-bandwidth system where the RF carrier frequency varies by a predetermined sequence. The receiver follows the same sequence, and jamming is hard.
Frequency hopping: a conventional carrier's center frequency changes many times per second, following a pseudo-random list of channels.
Direct sequence: the center stays fixed. A very fast pseudo-random code of chips smears the signal across a wide band.

blocks.title: Sharing a channel
items: TDMA (time division multiple access): a radio carries conversations one after another in separate time slots.
GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) shares a channel by Time Division Multiplex.
CDMA (code division multiple access): every call shares one wide band, each with its own code.
PCS (Personal Communications Systems): CDMA and GSM separate the calls.

blocks.title: Voice into bits
items: CODEC (coder/decoder): an IC or circuitry that converts voice into a predetermined digital format for encrypted transmission, and back.
GSM uses RPE, Regular-Pulse Excited: regular pulses drive a filter shaped like the throat and mouth.
Phase 2 P25 (Project 25) uses AMBE, Advanced Multi-Band Excitation.
ASCII has the widest acceptance for computer-to-computer data: 7 bits per character.

blocks.title: Packet radio: ISO 7-level model
items: Physical layer (1): actual transmission of data and handshaking signals.
Link layer (2): arranges bits into frames and controls data flow.

blocks.title: Radios in software
items: SDR (Software Defined Radio): filtering, modulation and demodulation run in software, so a new mode needs only new software.
DSP (digital signal processing) controls frequency, modulation and detection. It doesn't control SWR, standing wave ratio, set by the antenna match outside the radio.

blocks.title: Maritime codes
items: DSC (digital selective calling), part of GMDSS: a 10 bit error correcting code. The 3 check bits count the zeros in the data.
SITOR (simplex teletype over radio): each character is 7 bits. A character that breaks the 4 to 3 ratio is an error.
SITOR-A, ARQ: automatic repeat request; the receiver asks for repeats.
SITOR-B, FEC: forward error correction; every character is sent twice.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: AM, FM, QPSK, QAM and APSK are modulation types, not spreading methods.
TDMA isn't separate frequencies, pilot tones or power levels. GSM isn't frequency division.
DSC check bits come last. 7 data bits plus 1 parity bit is plain parity.
SITOR is 4 zeros and 3 ones, not the reverse or 5 bit Baudot.
Transport sits higher up. There's no communications or synchronization layer.
